articles/homeservers.html.title: Homeservers | Uniform MatrixRTC Authorization Server
articles/homeservers.html.summary: Homeservers Apps find the service through their homeserver, which announces it as a MatrixRTC focus. Announce the address the reverse proxy serves, such as https://example.org/livekit/jwt. Synapse Apps read the focus from /.well-known/matrix/client of your domain, which your web server usually serves for Synapse. Add the focus there: { "m.homeserver": { "base_url": "https://matrix.example.org" }, "org.matrix.msc4143.rtc_foci": [ { "type": "livekit", "livekit_service_url": "https://example.org/livekit/jwt" } ] } Uniform Chat Server Uniform Chat Server has this service built in, see its guide. To use a separate one instead, set Calls:MatrixRtcServiceUrl: { "Calls": { "MatrixRtcServiceUrl": "https://example.org/livekit/jwt" } } Users of other homeservers MatrixRtc:FullAccessHomeservers lists the homeservers whose users start calls. Users of other homeservers can join a call that one of them started, but only to watch and listen. List their servers as well to let them speak, or * for everyone. This service doesn't know who is in which room, so it gives a token to any verified user who asks for a room's call, as lk-jwt-service does. In encrypted rooms an outsider only receives encrypted media, as the apps send the call's keys to its members only. The service built into Uniform Chat Server also checks that the user is joined to the room. Leaving calls When a call app disappears without hanging up, for example when its phone loses the network, its homeserver ends the app's call membership after a delay. Apps such as Element X hand that delayed leave to this service. The service then ends the membership as soon as the SFU no longer sees the app, and the apps renew it far less often, which saves their battery. For this the service calls the homeserver of each member who handed over their leave, at https:// and the address the homeserver's /.well-known/matrix/client names. Let it reach your homeservers on port 443.

articles/running.html.title: Running | Uniform MatrixRTC Authorization Server
articles/running.html.summary: Running The service needs a LiveKit server with an API key, see LiveKit's self-hosting guide. Turn off LiveKit's room: auto_create, so that only users of full-access homeservers can start calls; the service creates their rooms. Install Unpack the release anywhere. On Debian and Ubuntu, the releases are also an apt repository, for x64 and arm64: add it once, with its signing key, then install the service, which sudo apt upgrade keeps up to date. The command is then uniform-matrixrtc-server in place of ./uniform-matrixrtc-server below. sudo install -d -m 0755 /etc/apt/keyrings curl -fsSL https://github.com/tagcode/Uniform.Chat/releases/latest/download/uniform-chat-archive-keyring.gpg | sudo tee /etc/apt/keyrings/uniform-chat.gpg > /dev/null echo "deb [signed-by=/etc/apt/keyrings/uniform-chat.gpg] https://github.com/tagcode/Uniform.Chat/releases/ latest/download/" | sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/uniform-chat.list sudo apt update sudo apt install uniform-matrixrtc-server First start Give the service LiveKit's address, its API key and secret, and your homeserver. Put the secret in the settings file or an environment variable, not on the command line, where other users of the computer can see it: export MatrixRtc__ApiSecret='a-long-random-secret-of-at-least-32-characters' ./uniform-matrixrtc-server --MatrixRtc:Url=wss://livekit.example.org --MatrixRtc:ApiKey=homeserver --MatrixRtc:FullAccessHomeservers=example.org It listens on port 8080. When a setting is missing, the service prints which one and stops. Apps reach it over HTTPS, so put a reverse proxy with a certificate in front of it. The usual path is /livekit/jwt of the homeserver's domain. With Caddy, for example: example.org { handle_path /livekit/jwt/* { reverse_proxy localhost:8080 } } https://example.org/livekit/jwt/healthz then answers with status 200. Settings come from, later ones overriding earlier ones: appsettings.json next to the program ~/.config/uniform-matrixrtc-server/settings.json The service's environment variables, such as MATRIXRTC_SECRET Environment variables, with __ between parts: MatrixRtc__ApiSecret The command line: --MatrixRtc:Url=wss://livekit.example.org Its log files are in ~/.local/share/uniform-matrixrtc-server/logs, one per start. As a system service Unpack it in /opt/uniform-matrixrtc-server, create a user for it, and write the settings, with the secret, to /etc/uniform-matrixrtc-server/settings.json: sudo useradd --system --home-dir /var/lib/uniform-matrixrtc-server --shell /usr/sbin/nologin uniform-matrixrtc-server sudo mkdir -p /opt/uniform-matrixrtc-server /etc/uniform-matrixrtc-server sudo tar -xzf uniform-chat-matrixrtc-<version>-linux-x64.tar.gz -C /opt/uniform-matrixrtc-server --strip-components=1 sudo nano /etc/uniform-matrixrtc-server/settings.json sudo chown -R uniform-matrixrtc-server:uniform-matrixrtc-server /etc/uniform-matrixrtc-server sudo chmod 600 /etc/uniform-matrixrtc-server/settings.json { "MatrixRtc": { "Url": "wss://livekit.example.org", "ApiKey": "homeserver", "ApiSecret": "a-long-random-secret-of-at-least-32-characters", "FullAccessHomeservers": "example.org" } } Then the unit file /etc/systemd/system/uniform-matrixrtc-server.service: [Unit] Description=Uniform MatrixRTC authorization server After=network-online.target Wants=network-online.target [Service] User=uniform-matrixrtc-server Group=uniform-matrixrtc-server ExecStart=/opt/uniform-matrixrtc-server/uniform-matrixrtc-server Environment=XDG_CONFIG_HOME=/etc Environment=XDG_DATA_HOME=/var/lib StateDirectory=uniform-matrixrtc-server Restart=on-failure NoNewPrivileges=true ProtectSystem=strict ProtectHome=true PrivateTmp=true ReadWritePaths=/var/lib/uniform-matrixrtc-server [Install] WantedBy=multi-user.target sudo systemctl daemon-reload sudo systemctl enable --now uniform-matrixrtc-server journalctl -u uniform-matrixrtc-server -f

articles/settings.html.title: Settings | Uniform MatrixRTC Authorization Server
articles/settings.html.summary: Settings The service's settings are in section MatrixRtc. Changes take effect at the next request, without a restart. Environment variables set the same settings, shown in the last column. They are lk-jwt-service's with MATRIXRTC_ in place of LIVEKIT_: when you move from lk-jwt-service, rename them. Option Default Meaning MatrixRtc:Enabled false Serve the endpoints; this program's appsettings.json sets it to true. MatrixRtc:Url not set Address of the LiveKit server that apps join, such as wss://livekit.example.org. MATRIXRTC_URL MatrixRtc:ApiKey not set API key of the LiveKit server, one of the keys in its configuration. MATRIXRTC_KEY or MATRIXRTC_KEY_FILE MatrixRtc:ApiSecret not set Secret of that API key. Keep it out of command lines. MATRIXRTC_SECRET or MATRIXRTC_SECRET_FILE MatrixRtc:FullAccessHomeservers not set Homeservers whose users may start calls and send audio and video, separated by commas, or * for all; users of other servers can only watch and listen in calls that are already going. Required. MATRIXRTC_FULL_ACCESS_HOMESERVERS MatrixRtc:TokenLifetime 01:00:00 How long an SFU token can be used to join; a call that has started goes on. MatrixRtc:CanUpdateOwnMetadata false Let participants change their own name and metadata on the SFU. Logging:LogLevel:Default Information Least important log entries written: Information logs every issued token, Warning only refusals. The address to listen on is Urls, http://0.0.0.0:8080 by default, or MATRIXRTC_JWT_BIND, such as :8080.

index.html.title: MatrixRTC authorization server | Uniform MatrixRTC Authorization Server
index.html.summary: Uniform MatrixRTC Authorization Server uniform-matrixrtc-server lets Element X, Element Call and other MatrixRTC apps join calls on your LiveKit server. An app proves who its user is with a Matrix OpenID token, and gets back an SFU token for the call's room. It replaces lk-jwt-service, with environment variables named like its own. Uniform Chat Server has the same service built in. Running: first start, and as a service. Settings: every setting. Homeservers: announcing it from Synapse or Uniform Chat Server.
